claims.text: The starting material is a modified CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy containing an optimized amount of vanadium.
The starting alloy has a homogeneous coarse-grained microstructure.
Laser surface alloying can rapidly melt and resolidify approximately the top 50 μm of the alloy.
Controlled laser processing produces a uniform nanoscale distribution of V-rich precipitates.
Rapid laser melting and resolidification induce nanoscale chemical heterogeneity and precipitation of V-rich regions.
The V-rich nanoprecipitates oxidize during sliding to form a vanadium oxide tribofilm.
The vanadium oxide tribofilm is lubricious and self-healing.
The vanadium oxide tribofilm reduces interfacial shear stress.
The vanadium oxide tribofilm enhances wear resistance.
Laser-treated material will exhibit a friction coefficient of approximately 0.2.
Laser treatment will decrease wear rate by approximately one order of magnitude relative to untreated material.
The friction and wear improvements will be sustained from 77 K to 800 K.
Untreated or non-laser-alloyed modified CoCrFeMnNi alloys typically have friction coefficients around 0.3.
Untreated modified CoCrFeMnNi alloys have higher wear rates than the proposed laser-treated material over the same temperature range.
The treatment remains effective within the engineered near-surface layer under ambient sliding conditions.
Treatment performance may be sensitive to deviations from optimized laser energy density and scanning speed.
The treatment's effect may not extend beneath the processed surface zone.
